title: New York's 23rd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for New York's 23rd Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Rep. Nick Langworthy against either Democrat Aaron Gies or Kevin Stocker, who are competing in the June 23 Democratic primary. The district covers Western New York and the Southern Tier, including all of Allegany, Cattaraugus, Chautauqua, Chemung, and Tioga counties and parts of Erie, Schuyler, and Steuben counties. This is a reliably Republican district — Donald Trump carried it by 21 points in 2024 — and the Cook Political Report rates the general election as Solid R. The race has centered on affordability, rural economic development, and Langworthy's voting record and constituent engagement.
polling_note: No publicly available opinion polls were found for the NY-23 2026 general or primary elections.

candidates.name: Nick Langworthy
candidates.summary: Nick Langworthy is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 23rd Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A former chairman of the New York Republican State Committee, he serves on the House Rules, Energy and Commerce, and Oversight Committees. Langworthy has prioritized constituent service, rural economic development, and fiscal conservatism, and advanced to the general election without a primary challenger.

candidates.name: Aaron Gies
candidates.summary: Aaron Gies is an associate professor of Theology and Franciscan Studies at St. Bonaventure University and a first-time candidate for office. He is running on the Democratic and Working Families Party lines, emphasizing affordability, community investment, and accountable government. Gies has been endorsed by five county Democratic committees in the district and has focused on town hall-style engagement with constituents.

candidates.name: Kevin Stocker
candidates.summary: Kevin Stocker is an attorney in Erie County with more than 35 years of legal experience, including service as a town prosecutor for Kenmore and Tonawanda. A former Republican who switched parties in 2016, he is running for Congress on a platform of fighting for hardworking families, protecting democracy, and holding political bosses accountable. Stocker has run for state office previously, including a 2020 Democratic primary bid for state assembly.
